body:
MEASURED on 2026-08-17 from a request trace of two different Anthropic clients against the live store.

WHAT HAPPENS. Both clients OPEN the conversation with `server/discover`, before `initialize`. Loam
answers `{"code":-32601,"message":"no such method server/discover"}`. One client (`Anthropic/Toolbox`)
tolerates the refusal and falls back to `initialize` — that path works today. The other
(`Anthropic/ClaudeAI`) treats it as a dead connection and stops, reporting only `Connection closed`,
and caches that state so it will not retry without a reconnect.

THE SPEC: `server/discover` is in the current MCP draft and servers **MUST** implement it. It lets a
client read supported protocol versions, capabilities and identity in one call, before any other
request. Verified at https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/server/discover .

THE RESPONSE SHAPE, from the spec's own example — do not invent it:
  result.resultType: "complete"
  result.supportedVersions: string[]        // the client picks one for subsequent requests
  result.capabilities: { tools: {}, ... }
  result._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]: { name, version }   // SHOULD be included
  result.instructions: string               // optional guidance for an LLM
  result.ttlMs / result.cacheScope          // optional, caching

EVERY VALUE MUST BE THE STORE'S OWN. `supportedVersions` is `MCP_PROTOCOLS` verbatim (today
["2025-06-18","2025-03-26"]) — NOT a version the store cannot speak. `capabilities` is what
`initialize` already answers. `serverInfo` is the same name and version `initialize` reports, which
`scripts/sync-version.mjs` keeps in step with package.json. A discover response that advertised more
than initialize honours would be a report that can be false (H7) on the store's own front step.

NOTE THE VERSION SEAM, because it is the reason to be careful rather than quick: the clients ask for
protocol `2025-11-25` and `2026-07-28`; the store speaks `2025-06-18` and negotiates down correctly at
`initialize`. This ticket does NOT add support for a newer revision. It reports honestly what is
supported, so a client can choose. If a client then demands a newer revision's semantics, that is a
separate ticket with a real feature in it.

RAILS (new file — check whether test/server/mcp-tool-honesty.test.ts, FROZEN by T86, enumerates
methods before adding anything near it):
1. `server/discover` answers a result whose `supportedVersions` EQUALS the exported `MCP_PROTOCOLS`,
   compared to the constant rather than to a copied literal, so the two cannot drift.
2. Its `capabilities` and `serverInfo` equal what `initialize` answers, asserted by calling both in
   one test and comparing — the anti-drift rail.
3. It works with NO token on a door that requires one? NO — assert the opposite: the method sits behind
   the same bearer requirement as the rest of the MCP door, and unauthenticated it answers the same
   401 with the same challenge. Discovery of the AUTH surface is the well-known documents' job (T177);
   this method is inside the door.
4. An unknown method still answers -32601, so the fix adds a method rather than making the door
   permissive.
5. A notification-shaped `server/discover` (no id) gets silence, like every other notification.

TIER: repair. It implements a MUST the store already had the values for, and discloses nothing
`initialize` did not. Self-merges on green plus P5.

PART OF THE CONNECTOR ARC: one of four before the debugging proxy comes down. See T176, T177, T148.

OVERTAKEN (stale sweep, 2026-08-25): PR #424 (commit 75a7407) implemented server/discover — case "server/discover" at src/server/http.ts:1189 on main, answering MCP_PROTOCOLS and initialize's own capabilities/serverInfo — with the ticket's rail test/server/mcp-discover.test.ts (228 lines). Shard still unarchived.
title: `server/discover` is unimplemented, and the spec says servers MUST implement it
